title: Prefetch-slab hit/latency sweep harness + regression detector for slab cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a reproducible performance sweep that maps slab cache hit rate -> p95 latency -> memory usage for the new slab-prefetcher shim. The goal is to produce an iso-latency hit-rate curve and integrate an automated regression detector into CI so future changes to prefetch heuristics or allocation sizing do not regress p95 or throughput unexpectedly. This ticket covers harness design, initial runs on our perf fleet, result analysis, and follow-up tasks (observability metrics and CI alerts).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can simulate configurable prefix distributions and emit workload with tokens/sec metadata
Sweep jobs produce CSV outputs with columns: hit_rate, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_sec, memory_mb
Iso-latency curve produced (hit_rate vs p95) and stored in perf S3
Regression detector (Jenkins + perf-checker) flags >8% p95 regressions or >10% tokens/sec drops relative to baseline
Instrumentation added: slab_prefetch_hits_total, slab_prefetch_misses_total, slab_lookup_latency_ms_bucket, tokens_processed_total
test_plan: Implement load generator plugin 'slab-sim' in loadlab to synthesize prefix reuse patterns and controlled hit rates
Add memory-pressure knob to simulate different slab allocations (2GB, 4GB, 8GB, 16GB)
Run baseline on runtime-1.21 image with existing prefetch disabled to capture baseline curves
Run sweep for forward-look prefetch v0.3 and backward-only prefetch v0.2 across hit_rate range 10%->95% in 10% increments
Collect token throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p95/p99 latencies, host memory RSS, and slab allocator stats per run
Run 5 samples per configuration and compute median and interquartile ranges
Push results to S3 and generate Grafana-compatible JSON for dashboarding
Add perf-checker job that compares new sweep aggregated p95 against baseline and fails PR if threshold exceeded
design_notes: We use a slab allocator abstraction in the runtime; the prefetch shim can pre-allocate small slabs for hot prefixes. To stress different regimes we will vary two orthogonal axes: (1) logical hit rate by controlling prefix reuse in the synthetic workload, (2) memory budget for slab pools. Observability will be at the per-request token granularity for latency histograms; regression detection uses distribution-aware checks (compute p95 + nonparametric KS/AD test on latency samples) but the CI gate will be a simple relative p95/tokens_sec threshold to avoid flaky false positives.
results_summary: Initial sweep on perf fleet (3-node cluster, a40-equivalent) produced the following high-level findings: forward-look prefetch v0.3 at 60% simulated hit rate reduced p95 from 42ms -> 26ms while increasing RSS by ~1.6GB. At very high hit rates (>90%) tokens/sec improved by +18%, p95 plateaued ~18ms, and additional slab memory gave diminishing returns. Regression detector prototype flagged a synthetic mutation (changed eviction order) which increased p95 by 12% at 40% hit rate — the alert correctly surfaced and linked to the PR that introduced the change. Full CSVs, plots, and dashboard are attached below.
